client.groups.acl
get# Copyclient.groups.acl.get(...) await client.groups.acl.get_async(...) Get the user access control list for a Worker Group, Outpost Group, or Edge Fleet.
Get the user access control list (ACL) for the specified Worker Group, Outpost Group, or Edge Fleet. This endpoint lists users with explicit access assignments on the Group or Fleet. The response does not include access granted through Team membership or inherited based on a user’s Permissions and Roles at the Organization/Global, Workspace, or product level. To list the Team ACL for a product and Group or Fleet, use GET /products/{product}/groups/{id}/acl/teams.
Example Usage# Copyresponse = client.groups.acl.get( id="example", ) Parameters# Parameter Type Required Default Description id str Yes — The id of the Worker Group, Outpost Group, or Edge Fleet to get the ACL for product Literal["stream", "edge", "outpost"] No "stream" Name of the Cribl product that contains the Worker Group, Outpost Group, or Edge Fleet. Valid values: “stream”, “edge”, “outpost” type Literal[…] | None (13 values)Literal["groups", "insights-apps", "datasets", "dataset-providers", "projects", "dashboards", "macros", "notebooks", "notebook-templates", "apps", "secret-folders", "ai-workflows", "ai-workflow-runs"] | None No — Filter for limiting the response to ACL entries for the specified RBAC resource type. Valid values: “groups”, “insights-apps”, “datasets”, “dataset-providers”, “projects”, “dashboards”, “macros”, “notebooks”, “notebook-templates”, “apps”, “secret-folders”, “ai-workflows”, “ai-workflow-runs” Response# SDKResponse
(200) PaginatedResponse containing a list of UserAccessControlList objects.
Copyresponse = client.groups.acl.get(...) for item in response.data.items: print(item) Errors# This operation may raise the following SDK exceptions.
Error Status Code Description AuthenticationError 401 Authentication failed (missing or invalid credentials or Bearer token). NotFoundError 404 Worker Group, Outpost Group, or Edge Fleet not found. ServerError 500 Unexpected server error. List user ACL for a Group — Response
Copy# Example response for listing the user access control list (ACL) for a Group. The response includes only users with explicit access assignments on the Group, not access granted through Team membership or inheritance. { "count": 1, "items": [ { "user": "user1@example.com", "perms": [{"type": "groups", "gid": "group1", "policy": "GroupRead"}], }, ], }

title: Captures
content:
System › Captures
system.captures
Capture operations
client.system.captures
create# Copyclient.system.captures.create(...) await client.system.captures.create_async(...) Capture live data as an NDJSON stream.
Initiate a live data capture from Cribl Workers. Yields CapturedEvent objects as they arrive over the wire (line-delimited JSON).
Example Usage# Copy# Example request body for capturing events by sourcetype. client.system.captures.create( filter="sourcetype===\"pan:traffic\"", maxEvents=100, duration=5, level=0, ) Parameters# Parameter Type Required Default Description duration int | None No 5 Amount of time to keep capture open, in seconds filter str | None No — JavaScript expression evaluated against each event to determine whether an event is included in the capture output. Expressions can reference any event field and use logical operators. If not provided, all events are captured level int | None No 0 Stage at which events are captured maxEvents int | None No 100 Maximum number of events to capture stepDuration int | None No 5 How long to wait before increasing the capture sample size. Specify 1 second or longer workerId str | None No — Unique ID of the Worker workerThreshold int | None No 50 Maximum number of Workers that can capture initially. A value of 0 means unlimited (all available Workers can capture) Response# Generator[CapturedEvent]
Copyfor event in client.system.captures.create(...): print(event) Errors# This operation may raise the following SDK exceptions.
Error Status Code Description ValidationError 400 Failed validation or malformed input — No worker nodes are connected to this worker group. AuthenticationError 401 Authentication failed (missing or invalid credentials or Bearer token). ServerError 500 Unexpected server error. Capture events using the AND operator to specify multiple conditions
Copy# Example request body for capturing events using the AND operator to specify multiple conditions. client.system.captures.create( filter="sourcetype===\"pan:traffic\" && src_zone===\"trusted\"", maxEvents=100, duration=5, level=0, ) Capture events using dot notation to specify nested fields
Copy# Example request body for capturing events using dot notation to specify nested fields. client.system.captures.create( filter="sourcetype===\"pan:traffic\" && dest_geoip.country.iso_code === \"US\"", maxEvents=100, duration=5, level=0, ) Capture with a complex filter that uses JavaScript methods
Copy# Example request body for capturing with a complex filter that uses JavaScript methods. client.system.captures.create( filter="__inputId.startsWith(\"http:\") && status >= 400 && status < 500", maxEvents=500, duration=15, level=1, ) Return one captured event — Response
Copy# Example response for streaming one captured event as an NDJSON line from a live data capture. { "_time": 1700000000, "_raw": "2023-11-14T22:13:20Z src=10.0.1.50 dst=192.168.1.100 action=allow", "sourcetype": "pan:traffic", "__inputId": "syslog:my_syslog_input", }

title: Cribl.Cloud OAuth2 client credentials flow · Cribl.Cloud
content:
Guides › Examples › Authentication Cribl.Cloud OAuth2 client credentials flow# Cribl.Cloud example_cloud_auth.py
Prerequisites# pip install cribl-python-sdk Environment variables# Variable Default CRIBL_CLOUD_URL https://your-workspace.cribl.cloud CRIBL_CLIENT_ID — CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET — Code# Python Line numbers Copy code Download .py 2import asyncio 3import os 4 5from cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security 6 7 8async def main() -> None: 9 # OAuth2 client credentials — SDK fetches and refreshes the token automatically. 10 # token_url and audience default to Cribl Cloud values from the OpenAPI spec. 11 cribl = Cribl( 12 server_url=os.getenv("CRIBL_CLOUD_URL", "https://your-workspace.cribl.cloud"), 13 security=Security( 14 client_id=os.getenv("CRIBL_CLIENT_ID", ""), 15 client_secret=os.getenv("CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET", ""), 16 ), 17 ) 18 19 # List pipelines (async) 20 resp = await cribl.pipelines.list_async() 21 print(f"Found {resp.data.count} pipeline(s)") 22 for p in resp.data.items: 23 print(f" - {p.id} (output: {p.conf.get('output', '-')})") 24 25 # Health check 26 health = await cribl.health.get_async() 27 print(f"\nHealth: {health.data.status}") 28 29 await cribl.close_async() 30 31 32if __name__ == "__main__": 33 asyncio.run(main())

title: Getting Started
content:
Getting Started# Install the SDK and make your first API call against Cribl.Cloud or an on-prem Leader. One Cribl client covers the control plane and the Cribl.Cloud platform API, with authentication and token refresh handled for you.
Install# Requires Python 3.14 or later.
uv Copyuv add cribl-python-sdk pip Copypip install cribl-python-sdk poetry Copypoetry add cribl-python-sdk Quickstart# A complete script: check server health, list Worker Groups, then list Sources and Pipelines in one group. Replace the placeholders with your own values.
Cribl.Cloud Copyfrom cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security with Cribl( server_url="https://main-your-org.cribl.cloud", # your Workspace URL security=Security(client_id="your-client-id", client_secret="your-client-secret"), ) as cribl: health = cribl.health.get() print(f"Server health: {health.data.status}") groups = cribl.groups.list() print(f"Found {groups.data.count} Worker Group(s)") # Control-plane calls scoped to one Worker Group with cribl.in_context(group_id="default") as wg: print(f"Found {wg.sources.list().data.count} Source(s)") print(f"Found {wg.pipelines.list().data.count} Pipeline(s)") # Cribl.Cloud platform API: same client, same credentials workspaces = cribl.cloud.workspaces.list(organization_id="your-org") print(f"Found {len(workspaces.data.items)} Workspace(s)") On-prem Copyfrom cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security with Cribl( server_url="http://localhost:9000", # your Leader URL security=Security(username="admin", password="admin"), ) as cribl: health = cribl.health.get() print(f"Server health: {health.data.status}") groups = cribl.groups.list() print(f"Found {groups.data.count} Worker Group(s)") # Control-plane calls scoped to one Worker Group with cribl.in_context(group_id="default") as wg: print(f"Found {wg.sources.list().data.count} Source(s)") print(f"Found {wg.pipelines.list().data.count} Pipeline(s)") Async# Every method has an _async twin. Use async with inside a coroutine and run it with asyncio.run():
Copyimport asyncio from cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security async def main() -> None: async with Cribl( server_url="http://localhost:9000", security=Security(username="admin", password="admin"), ) as cribl: health = await cribl.health.get_async() print(f"Server health: {health.data.status}") groups = await cribl.groups.list_async() print(f"Found {groups.data.count} Worker Group(s)") asyncio.run(main()) See examples/ for more usage patterns.
Reference for the methods used above: health.get, groups.list, sources.list, pipelines.list, cloud.workspaces.list, in_context.
Authentication# The SDK handles token acquisition and refresh automatically: pass credentials once in Security(...) and the client manages the rest. Every snippet below plugs into Cribl(server_url=..., security=security) as in the Quickstart.
Deployment Security(...) Authenticates On-prem username=, password= Control plane Cribl.Cloud client_id=, client_secret= Control plane and cribl.cloud.* Any bearer_auth= Whatever the token is valid for On-Prem (username/password)# The client calls POST /auth/login internally, stores the JWT, and refreshes it before expiry.
Copyfrom cribl_python_sdk import Security security = Security(username="admin", password="admin") Cloud — Control Plane (OAuth2)# OAuth2 client credentials flow. The SDK fetches and refreshes the access token automatically.
Copyfrom cribl_python_sdk import Security security = Security(client_id="your-client-id", client_secret="your-client-secret") Cloud — Management Plane (cribl.cloud.*)# Same client, same credentials. Management plane operations live under the cribl.cloud.* namespace and route to the gateway (https://gateway.cribl.cloud by default), while control-plane calls go to server_url.
Pre-existing Bearer Token# If you already have a token (e.g. from an external auth flow), pass it directly — no auto-login or refresh:
Copyfrom cribl_python_sdk import Security security = Security(bearer_auth="your-token") How the client is organized# API Where it runs SDK Control plane Your Cribl leader (server_url) — on-prem or Cribl.Cloud client.pipelines, client.sources, … Cribl.Cloud platform Cribl.Cloud gateway (https://gateway.cribl.cloud) client.cloud.* — workspaces, API credentials, billing On Cribl.Cloud, the same Security(client_id=..., client_secret=...) authenticates both. On-prem username/password authenticates the control plane only.
Scoped Client# Instead of manually constructing group/node URLs, use in_context(). Control-plane calls route to /api/v1/m/{group_id} automatically; cribl.cloud.* is unchanged (still the gateway).
Copyfrom cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security with Cribl( server_url="http://localhost:9000", security=Security(username="admin", password="admin"), ) as cribl, cribl.in_context(group_id="my_fleet") as wg: sources = wg.sources.list() destinations = wg.destinations.list() pipelines = wg.pipelines.list() Creating Resources# Pipelines take explicit keyword arguments:
Copyfrom cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security with Cribl( server_url="http://localhost:9000", security=Security(username="admin", password="admin"), ) as cribl, cribl.in_context(group_id="default") as wg: wg.pipelines.create(id="my_pipe", conf={"functions": []}) Sources, Destinations and Collectors accept either a typed model or a plain dict. Pick one:
Typed model Copyfrom cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security from cribl_python_sdk.models.inputs import InputSyslog with Cribl( server_url="http://localhost:9000", security=Security(username="admin", password="admin"), ) as cribl, cribl.in_context(group_id="default") as wg: wg.sources.create(InputSyslog(id="syslog_typed", host="0.0.0.0", udpPort=514)) Plain dict Copyfrom cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security with Cribl( server_url="http://localhost:9000", security=Security(username="admin", password="admin"), ) as cribl, cribl.in_context(group_id="default") as wg: wg.sources.create({"id": "syslog_dict", "type": "syslog", "host": "0.0.0.0", "udpPort": 514}) Environment Variables# Variable Description CRIBL_SERVER_URL On-prem server origin (e.g. http://localhost:9000) CRIBL_USERNAME On-prem login username CRIBL_PASSWORD On-prem login password CRIBL_CLOUD_URL Cribl.Cloud workspace origin for the control plane (e.g. https://main-your-org.cribl.cloud) CRIBL_CLOUD_GATEWAY_URL Platform/mgmt gateway override (default: https://gateway.cribl.cloud) CRIBL_CLIENT_ID OAuth2 client ID (Cloud control plane + cribl.cloud.*) CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET OAuth2 client secret (Cloud control plane + cribl.cloud.*) CRIBL_AUDIENCE OAuth2 audience (default: https://api.cribl.cloud) CRIBL_TOKEN_URL OAuth2 token endpoint (default: https://login.cribl.cloud/oauth/token) CRIBL_WORKER_GROUP_ID Target worker group ID CRIBL_ORGANIZATION_ID Cribl.Cloud organization id for cribl.cloud.* examples CRIBL_SDK_DEBUG Set to true to enable debug logging (zero-code activation) Advanced Usage# Shell and script usage with uv# Use in a Python shell:
Copyuvx --from cribl-python-sdk python Standalone script without a project:
Copy#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script # /// script # requires-python = ">=3.14" # dependencies = [ # "cribl-python-sdk", # ] # /// from cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security cribl = Cribl( server_url="http://localhost:9000", security=Security(username="admin", password="admin"), ) print(cribl.health.get().data.status) Run with uv run script.py.

title: Commits
content:
Versioning › Commits
versioning.commits
Commit operations
client.versioning.commits
Overview# Method Description create Create a new commit for pending changes to the Cribl configuration. diff Get the diff for a commit. get Get the diff and log message for a commit. list List the commit history. push Push local commits to the remote repository. revert Revert a commit in the local repository. undo Discard uncommitted (staged) changes. Operations# create# Copyclient.versioning.commits.create(...) await client.versioning.commits.create_async(...) Create a new commit for pending changes to the Cribl configuration.
Any merge conflicts indicated in the response must be resolved using Git. To commit only a subset of configuration changes, specify the files to include in the commit in the files array.
Example Usage# Copy# Example request body for committing all pending changes to the Cribl configuration. client.versioning.commits.create( message="Updated pipeline configuration for syslog parsing", ) Parameters# Parameter Type Required Description message str Yes Commit message to use for the new Git commit effective bool | None No If true, apply the commit to the group’s effective configuration. Requires a group context files list[str] | None No Array of file paths to include in the commit, relative to the configuration root. If omitted, all pending changes are committed Response# SDKResponse
(200) PaginatedResponse containing GitCommitSummary objects.
Copyresponse = client.versioning.commits.create(...) for item in response.data.items: print(item) Errors# This operation may raise the following SDK exceptions.
Error Status Code Description ValidationError 400 When effective: true is provided without a group context. AuthenticationError 401 Authentication failed (missing or invalid credentials or Bearer token). ServerError 500 Unexpected server error. Commit changes in specific files
Copy# Example request body for committing a subset of configuration changes to specific files. client.versioning.commits.create( message="Update Route and Pipeline for HTTP Sources", effective=True, files=[ "groups/default/local/cribl/pipelines/http_input/conf.yml", "groups/default/local/cribl/routes.yml", ], ) Commit created — Response
Copy# Example response for creating a new commit for pending configuration changes. {"count": 1, "items": [...]} # ... (see API docs for full payload) diff# Copyclient.versioning.commits.diff(...) await client.versioning.commits.diff_async(...) Get the diff for a commit.
Default is the latest commit (HEAD).
Example Usage# Copyresponse = client.versioning.commits.diff() Parameters# Parameter Type Required Description commit str | None No The Git commit hash to get the diff for filename str | None No The relative path of the file to get the diff for diffLineLimit int | None No Number of lines of the diff to return. Default is 1000. Set to 0 to return the full diff, regardless of the number of lines Response# SDKResponse
(200) PaginatedResponse containing the requested GitDiffResult.
Copyresponse = client.versioning.commits.diff(...) for item in response.data.items: print(item) Errors# This operation may raise the following SDK exceptions.
Error Status Code Description AuthenticationError 401 Authentication failed (missing or invalid credentials or Bearer token). ServerError 500 Unexpected server error. Diff for a commit — Response
Copy# Example response for getting the diff of changes in a commit. { "count": 1, "items": [ { "diffJson": [ { "oldName": "groups/default/local/cribl/pipelines/http_input/conf.yml", "newName": "groups/default/local/cribl/pipelines/http_input/conf.yml", "addedLines": 5, "deletedLines": 2, "isCombined": False, "isGitDiff": True, "language": "yml", "blocks": [], }, ], }, ], } get# Copyclient.versioning.commits.get(...) await client.versioning.commits.get_async(...) Get the diff and log message for a commit.
Default is the latest commit (HEAD).
Example Usage# Copyresponse = client.versioning.commits.get() Parameters# Parameter Type Required Description commit str | None No The Git commit hash to retrieve the diff and log message for filename str | None No The relative path of the file to get the diff and log message for diffLineLimit int | None No Number of lines of the diff to return. Default is 1000. Set to 0 to return the full diff, regardless of the number of lines Response# SDKResponse
(200) PaginatedResponse containing the requested GitShowResult.
Copyresponse = client.versioning.commits.get(...) for item in response.data.items: print(item) Errors# This operation may raise the following SDK exceptions.
Error Status Code Description AuthenticationError 401 Authentication failed (missing or invalid credentials or Bearer token). ServerError 500 Unexpected server error. Diff and log message for a commit — Response
Copy# Example response for getting the diff and log message for a commit. { "count": 1, "items": [ { "commitMessage": "Updated syslog pipeline configuration", "diffJson": [ { "oldName": "groups/default/local/cribl/pipelines/syslog/conf.yml", "newName": "groups/default/local/cribl/pipelines/syslog/conf.yml", "addedLines": 3, "deletedLines": 1, "isCombined": False, "isGitDiff": True, "language": "yml", "blocks": [], }, ], }, ], } list# Copyclient.versioning.commits.list(...) await client.versioning.commits.list_async(...) List the commit history.
Analogous to git log for the Cribl configuration, allowing you to audit and review changes over time.
Example Usage# Copyresponse = client.versioning.commits.list() Parameters# Parameter Type Required Description count int | None No Maximum number of commits to read from the commit history. When provided, offset and limit are applied to that read set offset int | None No Pagination offset limit int | None No Maximum number of items to return Response# SDKResponse
(200) PaginatedResponse containing GitLogResult objects.
Copyresponse = client.versioning.commits.list(...) for item in response.data.items: print(item) Errors# This operation may raise the following SDK exceptions.
Error Status Code Description AuthenticationError 401 Authentication failed (missing or invalid credentials or Bearer token). ServerError 500 Unexpected server error. List commit history — Response
Copy# Example response for listing the commit history of the Cribl configuration repository. { "count": 2, "items": [...], "offset": 0, "limit": 20, } # ... (see API docs for full payload) push# Copyclient.versioning.commits.push(...) await client.versioning.commits.push_async(...) Push local commits to the remote repository.
Push all local commits from the local repository to the remote repository. Requires at least one local commit that has not been pushed. Returns an error if the remote repository cannot be reached or the push is rejected.
Example Usage# Copyresponse = client.versioning.commits.push() Response# SDKResponse
(200) PaginatedResponse containing str objects.
Copyresponse = client.versioning.commits.push(...) for item in response.data.items: print(item) Errors# This operation may raise the following SDK exceptions.
Error Status Code Description AuthenticationError 401 Authentication failed (missing or invalid credentials or Bearer token). ServerError 500 Unexpected server error. Push result — Response
Copy# Example response for pushing local commits to the remote repository. { "count": 1, "items": [ "To https://github.com/example/cribl-config.git\n a1b2c3d..b2c3d4e main -> main", ], } revert# Copyclient.versioning.commits.revert(...) await client.versioning.commits.revert_async(...) Revert a commit in the local repository.
Revert a commit in the local repository by creating a new commit that undoes the changes introduced by the specified commit. Use the force field to proceed even when the working directory is not clean.
Example Usage# Copy# Example request body for reverting a specific commit. client.versioning.commits.revert( commit="a1b2c3d4e5f6", ) Parameters# Parameter Type Required Description commit str Yes SHA-1 hash of the commit to revert force bool | None No If true, force the revert even when the working directory is not clean. Otherwise, false message str | None No Custom message to use for the revert commit. If omitted, a default message is generated Response# SDKResponse
(200) PaginatedResponse containing GitRevertResult objects.
Copyresponse = client.versioning.commits.revert(...) for item in response.data.items: print(item) Errors# This operation may raise the following SDK exceptions.
Error Status Code Description AuthenticationError 401 Authentication failed (missing or invalid credentials or Bearer token). ServerError 500 Unexpected server error. Force revert a commit with a custom message
Copy# Example request body for force reverting a specific commit with a custom revert message. client.versioning.commits.revert( commit="a1b2c3d4e5f6", message="Revert commit due to misconfiguration in Pipeline settings", force=True, ) Revert result — Response
Copy# Example response for reverting a commit in the local repository. { "count": 1, "items": [ { "audit": { "id": "a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2", "files": { "modified": ["groups/default/local/cribl/pipelines/http_input/conf.yml"], }, }, "reverted": True, }, ], } undo# Copyclient.versioning.commits.undo(...) await client.versioning.commits.undo_async(...) Discard uncommitted (staged) changes.
Discard all uncommitted (staged) configuration changes, resetting the working directory to the last committed state. Use only if you are certain that you do not need to preserve your local changes. When applied globally (no group), triggers a Cribl restart to reload the reverted configuration. Returns false if the working directory is already clean.
Example Usage# Copyresponse = client.versioning.commits.undo() Response# SDKResponse
(200) PaginatedResponse containing bool objects.
Copyresponse = client.versioning.commits.undo(...) for item in response.data.items: print(item) Errors# This operation may raise the following SDK exceptions.
Error Status Code Description AuthenticationError 401 Authentication failed (missing or invalid credentials or Bearer token). ServerError 500 Unexpected server error. Undo result — Response
Copy# Example response for discarding uncommitted changes. {"count": 1, "items": [True]}

title: Cribl.Cloud platform authentication example · Cribl.Cloud
content:
Guides › Examples › Authentication Cribl.Cloud platform authentication example# Cribl.Cloud example_cloud_platform_auth.py
Validates OAuth2 against the Cribl.Cloud gateway: health check, then list Workspaces.
To get Client ID and Secret: https://docs.cribl.io/cribl-as-code/sdks-auth/#sdks-auth-cloud
This example is for Cribl.Cloud only. It calls cribl.cloud.* (gateway), not the control-plane /api/v1 APIs.
Prerequisites# pip install cribl-python-sdk CRIBL_CLIENT_ID, CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET CRIBL_ORGANIZATION_ID CRIBL_CLOUD_URL (workspace origin; still required by the client constructor) Environment variables# Variable Default CRIBL_CLIENT_ID your-client-id CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET your-client-secret CRIBL_ORGANIZATION_ID your-org-id CRIBL_CLOUD_URL https://main-your-org.cribl.cloud Code# Python Line numbers Copy code Download .py 17import asyncio 18import os 19 20from cribl_python_sdk import APIError, AuthenticationError, Cribl, RateLimitError, Security 21 22CLIENT_ID = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLIENT_ID", "your-client-id") 23CLIENT_SECRET = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET", "your-client-secret") 24ORG_ID = os.getenv("CRIBL_ORGANIZATION_ID", "your-org-id") 25CLOUD_URL = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLOUD_URL", "https://main-your-org.cribl.cloud") 26 27 28async def main() -> None: 29 cribl = Cribl( 30 server_url=CLOUD_URL, 31 security=Security(client_id=CLIENT_ID, client_secret=CLIENT_SECRET), 32 ) 33 try: 34 print("Cribl.Cloud platform client created") 35 36 health = await cribl.cloud.health.get_async() 37 print(f"Health check passed. Status: {health.data.status or 'unknown'}") 38 39 workspaces = await cribl.cloud.workspaces.list_async(ORG_ID) 40 items = workspaces.data.items 41 count = workspaces.data.count 42 if items: 43 print(f"Found {count} Workspace(s):") 44 else: 45 print(f"No Workspaces found for Organization {ORG_ID}") 46 for ws in items: 47 alias = f" ({ws.alias})" if ws.alias else "" 48 print(f" - {ws.workspaceId}{alias} - {ws.state} in {ws.region}") 49 except AuthenticationError: 50 print("Authentication failed. Check CRIBL_CLIENT_ID and CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET.") 51 except RateLimitError: 52 print("Rate limit reached. Try again in a few seconds.") 53 except APIError as exc: 54 print(f"Request failed: {exc.message}") 55 finally: 56 await cribl.close_async() 57 58 59if __name__ == "__main__": 60 asyncio.run(main())

title: How-to
content:
Beyond the Getting Started basics: paging through list results, handling errors, tuning retries and bringing your own HTTP client. Each snippet is self-contained.
Pagination# List operations return SDKResponse[PaginatedResponse[T]] (see PaginatedResponse). Most accept offset and limit; the page carries items, count and, when the server reports it, total_count.
Copyfrom cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security with Cribl( server_url="https://your-leader:9000", security=Security(bearer_auth="your-token"), ) as client: offset, limit = 0, 100 while True: page = client.collectors.list(offset=offset, limit=limit).data for job in page.items: print(job.id) offset += page.count if page.count < limit or (page.total_count is not None and offset >= page.total_count): break Errors# HTTP errors raise a subclass of APIError carrying status_code, message and the raw response:
Status Exception 401 AuthenticationError 403 AuthorizationError 404 NotFoundError 422 ValidationError 429 RateLimitError 5xx ServerError Transport failures raise ConnectionError or TimeoutError; a response that doesn’t match the expected model raises ResponseValidationError.
Copyfrom cribl_python_sdk import APIError, Cribl, NotFoundError, Security with Cribl( server_url="https://your-leader:9000", security=Security(bearer_auth="your-token"), ) as client: try: client.pipelines.get("missing") except NotFoundError: print("no such pipeline") except APIError as exc: print(exc.status_code, exc.message) Retries# Requests are retried with exponential backoff (backoff_factor ** attempt seconds), or after the server’s Retry-After / retry-after-ms delay when one is sent. Idempotent methods (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, DELETE) retry on 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504; POST and PATCH retry on 429 only.
Copyfrom cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, RetryConfig, Security client = Cribl( server_url="https://your-leader:9000", security=Security(bearer_auth="your-token"), retry_config=RetryConfig(max_attempts=5, backoff_factor=1.5), ) RetryConfig(max_attempts=1) disables retries.
Custom httpx client# Pass your own httpx.Client / httpx.AsyncClient for proxies, mTLS, event hooks or custom transports. It is used as-is for control-plane calls, so set base_url to the origin plus /api/v1; timeout and http2 then come from your client, not from Cribl(...).
Copyimport httpx from cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security client = Cribl( server_url="https://your-leader:9000", security=Security(bearer_auth="your-token"), http_client=httpx.Client(base_url="https://your-leader:9000/api/v1", proxy="http://proxy.internal:3128", verify="/etc/ssl/corp-ca.pem"), async_http_client=httpx.AsyncClient(base_url="https://your-leader:9000/api/v1", proxy="http://proxy.internal:3128", verify="/etc/ssl/corp-ca.pem"), ) Set debug=True (optionally with debug_logger=) to log requests and responses; credentials are masked.

title: On-premises login flow · On-prem
content:
Guides › Examples › Authentication On-premises login flow# On-prem example_onprem_auth.py
Authenticate with username/password, then use the token.
Prerequisites# pip install cribl-python-sdk Environment variables# Variable Default CRIBL_SERVER_URL http://localhost:9000 CRIBL_USERNAME admin CRIBL_PASSWORD admin Code# Python Line numbers Copy code Download .py 2import os 3 4from cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security 5 6 7def main() -> None: 8 server_url = os.getenv("CRIBL_SERVER_URL", "http://localhost:9000") 9 username = os.getenv("CRIBL_USERNAME", "admin") 10 password = os.getenv("CRIBL_PASSWORD", "admin") 11 12 # Login to get a bearer token 13 cribl = Cribl(server_url=server_url) 14 token = cribl.auth.tokens.get(username=username, password=password) 15 16 # Create authenticated client (or use set_token) 17 cribl = Cribl( 18 server_url=server_url, 19 security=Security(bearer_auth=token.data.token), 20 ) 21 22 # List worker groups 23 resp = cribl.groups.list(product="stream") 24 print(f"Found {resp.data.count} worker group(s)") 25 for g in resp.data.items: 26 print(f" - {g.id} ({g.description or 'no description'})") 27 28 # Use in_context client for group-level operations 29 if resp.data.items: 30 with cribl.in_context(group_id=resp.data.items[0].id) as wg: 31 sources = wg.sources.list() 32 print(f"\nSources in group '{resp.data.items[0].id}': {sources.data.count}") 33 for s in sources.data.items: 34 print(f" - {s.id} ({s.type})") 35 36 cribl.close() 37 38 39if __name__ == "__main__": 40 main()

title: Create a Worker Group and deploy it · Cribl.Cloud
content:
Guides › Examples › Worker Groups Create a Worker Group and deploy it# Cribl.Cloud example_cloud_create_worker_group.py
This example is for Cribl.Cloud deployments only.
Prerequisites# pip install cribl-python-sdk CRIBL_CLIENT_ID and CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET env vars CRIBL_CLOUD_URL env var Environment variables# Variable Default CRIBL_CLIENT_ID your-client-id CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET your-client-secret CRIBL_CLOUD_URL https://main-your-org.cribl.cloud CRIBL_WORKER_GROUP_ID my-worker-group Code# Python Line numbers Copy code Download .py 10import asyncio 11import os 12 13from cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security 14 15 16CLIENT_ID = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLIENT_ID", "your-client-id") 17CLIENT_SECRET = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET", "your-client-secret") 18CLOUD_URL = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLOUD_URL", "https://main-your-org.cribl.cloud") 19WORKER_GROUP_ID = os.getenv("CRIBL_WORKER_GROUP_ID", "my-worker-group") 20 21 22async def main(): 23 cribl = Cribl( 24 server_url=CLOUD_URL, 25 security=Security( 26 client_id=CLIENT_ID, 27 client_secret=CLIENT_SECRET, 28 ), 29 ) 30 31 cribl.groups.create( 32 id=WORKER_GROUP_ID, 33 name="my-worker-group", 34 description="Cribl.Cloud Worker Group", 35 onPrem=False, 36 workerRemoteAccess=True, 37 ) 38 print(f"Worker Group created: {WORKER_GROUP_ID}") 39 40 with cribl.in_context(group_id=WORKER_GROUP_ID) as wg: 41 resp = wg.versioning.commits.create( 42 message="Commit for create Worker Group", 43 effective=True, 44 ) 45 commit = resp.data.items[0] 46 print(f"Committed: {commit.commit}") 47 48 assert commit.commit is not None 49 cribl.groups.deploy(id=WORKER_GROUP_ID, version=commit.commit) 50 print(f"Deployed: {WORKER_GROUP_ID}") 51 52 await cribl.close_async() 53 54 55if __name__ == "__main__": 56 try: 57 asyncio.run(main()) 58 except Exception as error: 59 print(f"Error: {error}")

Manage Cribl Lake Datasets.

Overview# Method Description create Create Lake Datasets (Cribl.Cloud only). delete Delete a Lake Dataset (Cribl.Cloud only). get Get a Lake Dataset (Cribl.Cloud only). list List all Lake Datasets (Cribl.Cloud only). update Update a Lake Dataset (Cribl.Cloud only). Operations# create# Copyclient.datasets.create(...) await client.datasets.create_async(...) Create Lake Datasets (Cribl.Cloud only).
Creates one or more Lake Datasets in the specified Lake in a single transaction (Cribl.Cloud only). Send a single Lake Dataset object to create just one, or an array to bulk-create multiple. When an array is sent, the response is { items, errors } – items contains the successfully created Lake Datasets, and errors contains an entry ({ id, reason }) for each Lake Dataset that failed validation, so a per-item failure does not fail the rest of the batch.
Example Usage# Copy# Example request body for creating a Lake Dataset in JSON format with a 90-day retention period. client.datasets.create( id="web_access_logs", description="Web server access logs", storageLocationId="my-storage-location", format="json", retentionPeriodInDays=90, acceleratedFields=[ "host", "status", ], ) Parameters# Parameter Type Required Description lakeId str Yes The id of the Lake to create the Lake Datasets in id str Yes Unique identifier for the Dataset acceleratedFields list[str] | None No Accelerated fields for the Dataset. Data is partitioned by these fields in storage to improve query performance allowRecordErasure bool | None No If true, the Dataset is opted in to Lake Record Erasure bucketName str | None No Name of the legacy Cribl Lake bucket that backs the Dataset. Mutually exclusive with storageLocationId cacheConnection CacheConnectionParam | None No Lakehouse cache connection settings for the Dataset deletionStartedAt int | None No Timestamp (in Unix time) when Dataset deletion was initiated, in milliseconds description str | None No Brief description of the Dataset format str | None No Storage format used for data persisted in the Dataset httpDAUsed bool | None No If true, the Dataset is used by Direct Access HTTP. Otherwise, false metrics DatasetMetricsParam | None No Most recent Dataset metrics snapshot providerPath str | None No Storage path within the provider (for example an S3 prefix or Azure container) retentionPeriodInDays int | None No Dataset retention period, in days searchConfig DatasetSearchConfigParam | None No Search configuration for the Dataset storageClass str | None No Storage class used for objects written to the Dataset storageLocationId str | None No Unique identifier for the Storage Location that backs the Dataset. Mutually exclusive with bucketName viewName str | None No Name of the ClickHouse view for the Dataset on the Lakehouse Response# SDKResponse
(200) PaginatedResponse containing the created CriblLakeDataset.
Copyresponse = client.datasets.create(...) for item in response.data.items: print(item) Errors# This operation may raise the following SDK exceptions.

title: List all Worker Groups in Cribl Stream · Cribl.Cloud
content:
Guides › Examples › Worker Groups List all Worker Groups in Cribl Stream# Cribl.Cloud example_cloud_list_worker_groups.py
This example is for Cribl.Cloud deployments only.
Prerequisites# pip install cribl-python-sdk CRIBL_CLIENT_ID and CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET env vars CRIBL_CLOUD_URL env var Environment variables# Variable Default CRIBL_CLIENT_ID your-client-id CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET your-client-secret CRIBL_CLOUD_URL https://main-your-org.cribl.cloud Code# Python Line numbers Copy code Download .py 10import asyncio 11import os 12 13from cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security 14 15 16CLIENT_ID = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLIENT_ID", "your-client-id") 17CLIENT_SECRET = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET", "your-client-secret") 18CLOUD_URL = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLOUD_URL", "https://main-your-org.cribl.cloud") 19 20 21async def main(): 22 cribl = Cribl( 23 server_url=CLOUD_URL, 24 security=Security( 25 client_id=CLIENT_ID, 26 client_secret=CLIENT_SECRET, 27 ), 28 ) 29 30 resp = await cribl.groups.list_async(product="stream") 31 if resp.data.items: 32 print(f"Worker Groups ({resp.data.count}):") 33 for g in resp.data.items: 34 print(f" {g.id} — {g.description or '(no description)'}") 35 else: 36 print("No Worker Groups found.") 37 38 await cribl.close_async() 39 40 41if __name__ == "__main__": 42 try: 43 asyncio.run(main()) 44 except Exception as error: 45 print(f"Error: {error}")

title: Replicate a Worker Group · Cribl.Cloud
content:
Guides › Examples › Worker Groups Replicate a Worker Group# Cribl.Cloud example_cloud_replicate_worker_group.py
Clone configuration from an existing group.
This example is for Cribl.Cloud deployments only.
Prerequisites# pip install cribl-python-sdk CRIBL_CLIENT_ID and CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET env vars CRIBL_CLOUD_URL env var An existing source Worker Group Environment variables# Variable Default CRIBL_CLIENT_ID your-client-id CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET your-client-secret CRIBL_CLOUD_URL https://main-your-org.cribl.cloud CRIBL_SOURCE_GROUP my-worker-group CRIBL_REPLICA_GROUP my-replica-group Code# Python Line numbers Copy code Download .py 11import asyncio 12import os 13 14from cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security 15 16 17CLIENT_ID = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLIENT_ID", "your-client-id") 18CLIENT_SECRET = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET", "your-client-secret") 19CLOUD_URL = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLOUD_URL", "https://main-your-org.cribl.cloud") 20SOURCE_GROUP = os.getenv("CRIBL_SOURCE_GROUP", "my-worker-group") 21REPLICA_GROUP = os.getenv("CRIBL_REPLICA_GROUP", "my-replica-group") 22 23 24async def main(): 25 cribl = Cribl( 26 server_url=CLOUD_URL, 27 security=Security( 28 client_id=CLIENT_ID, 29 client_secret=CLIENT_SECRET, 30 ), 31 ) 32 33 cribl.groups.create( 34 id=REPLICA_GROUP, 35 name="my-replica-worker-group", 36 description=f"Cloned from {SOURCE_GROUP}", 37 onPrem=False, 38 workerRemoteAccess=True, 39 sourceGroupId=SOURCE_GROUP, 40 ) 41 print(f"Replicated: {REPLICA_GROUP} (from {SOURCE_GROUP})") 42 43 with cribl.in_context(group_id=REPLICA_GROUP) as wg: 44 resp = wg.versioning.commits.create( 45 message="Commit for replicate Worker Group", 46 effective=True, 47 ) 48 commit = resp.data.items[0] 49 50 assert commit.commit is not None 51 cribl.groups.deploy(id=REPLICA_GROUP, version=commit.commit) 52 print(f"Deployed: {REPLICA_GROUP}") 53 54 await cribl.close_async() 55 56 57if __name__ == "__main__": 58 try: 59 asyncio.run(main()) 60 except Exception as error: 61 print(f"Error: {error}")

title: Replicate a Worker Group · On-prem
content:
Guides › Examples › Worker Groups Replicate a Worker Group# On-prem example_onprem_replicate_worker_group.py
Clone from an existing group.
This example is for on-prem deployments only.
Prerequisites# pip install cribl-python-sdk CRIBL_SERVER_URL, CRIBL_USERNAME, CRIBL_PASSWORD env vars An existing source Worker Group Environment variables# Variable Default CRIBL_SERVER_URL http://localhost:9000 CRIBL_USERNAME admin CRIBL_PASSWORD admin CRIBL_SOURCE_GROUP my-worker-group CRIBL_REPLICA_GROUP my-replica-group Code# Python Line numbers Copy code Download .py 10import asyncio 11import os 12 13from cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security 14SERVER_URL = os.getenv("CRIBL_SERVER_URL", "http://localhost:9000") 15USERNAME = os.getenv("CRIBL_USERNAME", "admin") 16PASSWORD = os.getenv("CRIBL_PASSWORD", "admin") 17SOURCE_GROUP = os.getenv("CRIBL_SOURCE_GROUP", "my-worker-group") 18REPLICA_GROUP = os.getenv("CRIBL_REPLICA_GROUP", "my-replica-group") 19async def main(): 20 cribl = Cribl(server_url=SERVER_URL) 21 token = cribl.auth.tokens.get(username=USERNAME, password=PASSWORD) 22 23 cribl = Cribl( 24 server_url=SERVER_URL, 25 security=Security(bearer_auth=token.data.token), 26 ) 27 28 cribl.groups.create( 29 id=REPLICA_GROUP, 30 name="my-replica-worker-group", 31 description=f"Cloned from {SOURCE_GROUP}", 32 onPrem=True, 33 workerRemoteAccess=True, 34 sourceGroupId=SOURCE_GROUP, 35 ) 36 print(f"Replicated: {REPLICA_GROUP} (from {SOURCE_GROUP})") 37 38 with cribl.in_context(group_id=REPLICA_GROUP) as wg: 39 resp = wg.versioning.commits.create( 40 message="Commit for replicate Worker Group", 41 effective=True, 42 ) 43 commit = resp.data.items[0] 44 45 assert commit.commit is not None 46 cribl.groups.deploy(id=REPLICA_GROUP, version=commit.commit) 47 print(f"Deployed: {REPLICA_GROUP}") 48 49 cribl.close() 50if __name__ == "__main__": 51 try: 52 asyncio.run(main()) 53 except Exception as error: 54 print(f"Error: {error}")

title: Scale Worker Processes · On-prem
content:
Guides › Examples › Worker Groups Scale Worker Processes# On-prem example_onprem_scale_worker_group.py
Optimize CPU/memory settings for a Worker Group.
This example is for on-prem deployments only.
Prerequisites# pip install cribl-python-sdk CRIBL_SERVER_URL, CRIBL_USERNAME, CRIBL_PASSWORD env vars An existing Worker Group Environment variables# Variable Default CRIBL_SERVER_URL http://localhost:9000 CRIBL_USERNAME admin CRIBL_PASSWORD admin CRIBL_WORKER_GROUP_ID default Code# Python Line numbers Copy code Download .py 10import asyncio 11import os 12 13from cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security 14SERVER_URL = os.getenv("CRIBL_SERVER_URL", "http://localhost:9000") 15USERNAME = os.getenv("CRIBL_USERNAME", "admin") 16PASSWORD = os.getenv("CRIBL_PASSWORD", "admin") 17WORKER_GROUP_ID = os.getenv("CRIBL_WORKER_GROUP_ID", "default") 18async def main(): 19 cribl = Cribl(server_url=SERVER_URL) 20 token = cribl.auth.tokens.get(username=USERNAME, password=PASSWORD) 21 22 cribl = Cribl( 23 server_url=SERVER_URL, 24 security=Security(bearer_auth=token.data.token), 25 ) 26 27 with cribl.in_context(group_id=WORKER_GROUP_ID) as wg: 28 # Get current settings 29 resp = wg.system.settings.cribl.list() 30 settings = resp.data.items[0] 31 print(f"Current workers config: {(settings.model_extra or {}).get('workers', {})}") 32 33 # Update worker process settings 34 wg.system.settings.cribl.update( 35 workers={"count": -3, "memory": 2048, "minimum": 2} 36 ) 37 print("Worker Process settings updated") 38 39 # Commit and deploy 40 resp = wg.versioning.commits.create( 41 message="Optimize Worker Process settings", 42 effective=True, 43 ) 44 commit = resp.data.items[0] 45 print(f"Committed: {commit.commit}") 46 47 assert commit.commit is not None 48 cribl.groups.deploy(id=WORKER_GROUP_ID, version=commit.commit) 49 print(f"Deployed: {WORKER_GROUP_ID}") 50 51 cribl.close() 52if __name__ == "__main__": 53 try: 54 asyncio.run(main()) 55 except Exception as error: 56 print(f"Error: {error}")

Fields# Field Type Required Description name str Yes Human-readable name of the API Credential. description str Yes Brief description of the purpose and usage for the API Credential. enabled bool Yes If true, the API Credential is enabled. An empty array means that the API Credential has no IP restrictions. createdBy str Yes Member who created the API Credential. createdDate str Yes ISO 8601 timestamp when the API Credential was created. lastUpdatedBy str Yes Member who last updated the API Credential. lastUpdatedDate str Yes ISO 8601 timestamp when the API Credential was last updated. clientSecret str Yes Client Secret for the API Credential. Prerequisites# pip install cribl-python-sdk CRIBL_CLIENT_ID and CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET env vars CRIBL_CLOUD_URL env var AWS credentials for the S3 destination Environment variables# Variable Default CRIBL_CLIENT_ID your-client-id CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET your-client-secret CRIBL_CLOUD_URL https://main-your-org.cribl.cloud CRIBL_WORKER_GROUP_ID my-group AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID your-aws-key AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY your-aws-secret AWS_BUCKET_NAME your-bucket AWS_REGION us-east-2 Code# Python Line numbers Copy code Download .py 11import asyncio 12import os 13 14from cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security 15from cribl_python_sdk.models import InputSyslog, OutputS3 16 17 18CLIENT_ID = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLIENT_ID", "your-client-id") 19CLIENT_SECRET = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET", "your-client-secret") 20CLOUD_URL = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLOUD_URL", "https://main-your-org.cribl.cloud") 21WORKER_GROUP_ID = os.getenv("CRIBL_WORKER_GROUP_ID", "my-group") 22AWS_API_KEY = os.getenv("AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID", "your-aws-key") 23AWS_SECRET_KEY = os.getenv("AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY", "your-aws-secret") 24AWS_BUCKET = os.getenv("AWS_BUCKET_NAME", "your-bucket") 25AWS_REGION = os.getenv("AWS_REGION", "us-east-2") 26 27 28async def main(): 29 cribl = Cribl( 30 server_url=CLOUD_URL, 31 security=Security( 32 client_id=CLIENT_ID, 33 client_secret=CLIENT_SECRET, 34 ), 35 ) 36 37 # Create worker group 38 cribl.groups.create( 39 id=WORKER_GROUP_ID, 40 name=WORKER_GROUP_ID, 41 onPrem=False, 42 ) 43 print(f"Worker Group created: {WORKER_GROUP_ID}") 44 45 with cribl.in_context(group_id=WORKER_GROUP_ID) as wg: 46 # Syslog source 47 wg.sources.create(InputSyslog.model_validate({"id": "in-syslog-9021", "type": "syslog", "host": "0.0.0.0", "port": 9021})) 48 print("Syslog source created: in-syslog-9021") 49 50 # S3 destination 51 wg.destinations.create(OutputS3.model_validate({ 52 "id": "out_s3", 53 "type": "s3", 54 "bucket": AWS_BUCKET, 55 "stagePath": "/tmp/cribl_stage", 56 "region": AWS_REGION, 57 "awsSecretKey": AWS_SECRET_KEY, 58 "awsApiKey": AWS_API_KEY, 59 "compress": "gzip", 60 })) 61 print("S3 destination created: out_s3") 62 63 # Pipeline with eval function 64 wg.pipelines.create( 65 id="my_pipeline", 66 conf={ 67 "asyncFuncTimeout": 1000, 68 "functions": [ 69 { 70 "id": "eval", 71 "filter": "true", 72 "conf": {"remove": ["*"], "keep": ["eventSource", "eventID"]}, 73 "final": True, 74 } 75 ], 76 }, 77 ) 78 print("Pipeline created: my_pipeline") 79 80 # Add a route to the default routing table 81 wg.routes.append( 82 "default", 83 routes=[{ 84 "name": "my_route", 85 "filter": "__inputId=='in-syslog-9021'", 86 "pipeline": "my_pipeline", 87 "output": "out_s3", 88 "description": "Route syslog to S3", 89 "final": True, 90 }], 91 ) 92 print("Route added") 93 94 # Commit and deploy 95 resp = wg.versioning.commits.create(message="Configure resources", effective=True) 96 commit = resp.data.items[0] 97 print(f"Committed: {commit.commit}") 98 99 assert commit.commit is not None 100 cribl.groups.deploy(id=WORKER_GROUP_ID, version=commit.commit) 101 print(f"Deployed: {WORKER_GROUP_ID}") 102 103 await cribl.close_async() 104 105 106if __name__ == "__main__": 107 try: 108 asyncio.run(main()) 109 except Exception as error: 110 print(f"Error: {error}")

title: ApiCredentialResponseSchema
content:
API Credential returned by list and get operations.
Fields# Field Type Required Description name str Yes Human-readable name of the API Credential. description str Yes Brief description of the purpose and usage for the API Credential. enabled bool Yes If true, the API Credential is enabled. Otherwise, false. organizationId str Yes Unique ID of the Organization. clientId str Yes Client ID for the API Credential. roles ApiCredentialRolesSchema Yes Role assignments for the API Credential. ipAllowlist list[str] Yes CIDR range enforced as the IP allowlist for the API Credential. An empty array means that the API Credential has no IP restrictions. createdBy str Yes Member who created the API Credential. createdDate str Yes ISO 8601 timestamp when the API Credential was created. lastUpdatedBy str Yes Member who last updated the API Credential. lastUpdatedDate str Yes ISO 8601 timestamp when the API Credential was last updated. Used by# client.cloud.api_credentials.get() Example# Copyfrom cribl_python_sdk.models import ApiCredentialResponseSchema obj = ApiCredentialResponseSchema( name="example", description="example", enabled=True, organizationId="example", clientId="example", roles={"organizationRole": "owner"}, ipAllowlist=["example"], createdBy="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", createdDate="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", lastUpdatedBy="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", lastUpdatedDate="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", )

title: Pack management example · Cribl.Cloud
content:
Guides › Examples › Configuration & Deployment Pack management example# Cribl.Cloud example_cloud_packs.py
Prerequisites# pip install cribl-python-sdk Environment variables# Variable Default CRIBL_SERVER_URL http://localhost:9000 CRIBL_USERNAME admin CRIBL_PASSWORD admin Code# Python Line numbers Copy code Download .py 2import os 3 4from cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security 5def main() -> None: 6 server_url = os.getenv("CRIBL_SERVER_URL", "http://localhost:9000") 7 8 cribl = Cribl(server_url=server_url) 9 token = cribl.auth.tokens.get( 10 username=os.getenv("CRIBL_USERNAME", "admin"), 11 password=os.getenv("CRIBL_PASSWORD", "admin"), 12 ) 13 14 cribl = Cribl( 15 server_url=server_url, 16 security=Security(bearer_auth=token.data.token), 17 ) 18 19 # List installed packs 20 resp = cribl.packs.list() 21 print(f"Installed packs ({resp.data.count}):") 22 for p in resp.data.items: 23 print(f" {p.id} v{p.version} — {p.description or '(no description)'}") 24 25 cribl.close() 26if __name__ == "__main__": 27 main()

Prerequisites# pip install cribl-python-sdk CRIBL_SERVER_URL, CRIBL_USERNAME, CRIBL_PASSWORD env vars A Worker Group with pending changes Environment variables# Variable Default CRIBL_SERVER_URL http://localhost:9000 CRIBL_USERNAME admin CRIBL_PASSWORD admin CRIBL_WORKER_GROUP_ID default Code# Python Line numbers Copy code Download .py 10import asyncio 11import os 12 13from cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security 14SERVER_URL = os.getenv("CRIBL_SERVER_URL", "http://localhost:9000") 15USERNAME = os.getenv("CRIBL_USERNAME", "admin") 16PASSWORD = os.getenv("CRIBL_PASSWORD", "admin") 17WORKER_GROUP_ID = os.getenv("CRIBL_WORKER_GROUP_ID", "default") 18async def main(): 19 cribl = Cribl(server_url=SERVER_URL) 20 token = cribl.auth.tokens.get(username=USERNAME, password=PASSWORD) 21 22 cribl = Cribl( 23 server_url=SERVER_URL, 24 security=Security(bearer_auth=token.data.token), 25 ) 26 27 with cribl.in_context(group_id=WORKER_GROUP_ID) as wg: 28 resp = wg.versioning.commits.create( 29 message="Commit for Cribl Stream example", 30 effective=True, 31 ) 32 commit = resp.data.items[0] 33 print(f"Committed: {commit.commit}") 34 35 assert commit.commit is not None 36 cribl.groups.deploy(id=WORKER_GROUP_ID, version=commit.commit) 37 print(f"Deployed: {WORKER_GROUP_ID}") 38 39 cribl.close() 40if __name__ == "__main__": 41 try: 42 asyncio.run(main()) 43 except Exception as error: 44 print(f"Error: {error}")

title: Scoped operations · On-prem
content:
Guides › Examples › Configuration & Deployment Scoped operations# On-prem example_onprem_configure_resources.py
Access resources within a worker group context.
Prerequisites# pip install cribl-python-sdk Environment variables# Variable Default CRIBL_SERVER_URL http://localhost:9000 CRIBL_USERNAME admin CRIBL_PASSWORD admin Code# Python Line numbers Copy code Download .py 2import os 3 4from cribl_python_sdk import Cribl, Security 5def main() -> None: 6 server_url = os.getenv("CRIBL_SERVER_URL", "http://localhost:9000") 7 8 cribl = Cribl(server_url=server_url) 9 token = cribl.auth.tokens.get( 10 username=os.getenv("CRIBL_USERNAME", "admin"), 11 password=os.getenv("CRIBL_PASSWORD", "admin"), 12 ) 13 14 cribl = Cribl( 15 server_url=server_url, 16 security=Security(bearer_auth=token.data.token), 17 ) 18 19 # Get first worker group 20 resp = cribl.groups.list(product="stream") 21 if not resp.data.items: 22 print("No worker groups found") 23 return 24 print(f"Using worker group: {resp.data.items[0].id}") 25 26 # Scope the client — all subsequent calls route to /m/{group_id} 27 with cribl.in_context(group_id=resp.data.items[0].id) as wg: 28 # List sources in this group 29 resp = wg.sources.list() 30 print(f"
Sources ({resp.data.count}):") 31 for s in resp.data.items: 32 print(f" {s.id}: {s.type}") 33 34 # List destinations in this group 35 resp = wg.destinations.list() 36 print(f"
Destinations ({resp.data.count}):") 37 for d in resp.data.items: 38 print(f" {d.id}: {d.type}") 39 40 # List pipelines in this group 41 resp = wg.pipelines.list() 42 print(f"
Pipelines ({resp.data.count}):") 43 for p in resp.data.items: 44 print(f" {p.id}") 45 46 # Create a pipeline (flattened kwargs — no model class needed) 47 resp = wg.pipelines.create( 48 id="sdk_test_pipeline", 49 conf={"functions": [{"id": "comment", "conf": {"comment": "Created by SDK"}}]}, 50 ) 51 print(f"
Created pipeline: {resp.data.items[0].id}") 52 53 # Clean up 54 wg.pipelines.delete("sdk_test_pipeline") 55 print("Deleted test pipeline") 56 57 cribl.close() 58if __name__ == "__main__": 59 main()

title: Create a Cribl.Cloud API Credential (Organization Admin) · Cribl.Cloud
content:
Guides › Examples › Cribl.Cloud Platform Create a Cribl.Cloud API Credential (Organization Admin)# Cribl.Cloud example_cloud_api_credential_organization_admin.py
Creates a new API Credential with the Admin role on the Organization. That role applies across the Organization, including all Workspaces and products (no Workspace or product matrix is required).
The create response includes clientSecret once. Do not print or log it. Store it securely if you will use the new credential later.
https://docs.cribl.io/cribl-as-code/sdks-auth/#sdks-auth-cloud
This example is for Cribl.Cloud only (cribl.cloud.api_credentials).
Prerequisites# pip install cribl-python-sdk CRIBL_CLIENT_ID, CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET (an existing API Credential, to authenticate) CRIBL_ORGANIZATION_ID CRIBL_CLOUD_URL (workspace origin; still required by the client constructor) Environment variables# Variable Default CRIBL_CLIENT_ID your-client-id CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET your-client-secret CRIBL_ORGANIZATION_ID your-org-id CRIBL_CLOUD_URL https://main-your-org.cribl.cloud Code# Python Line numbers Copy code Download .py 20import os 21 22from cribl_python_sdk import APIError, AuthenticationError, Cribl, RateLimitError, Security 23 24CLIENT_ID = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLIENT_ID", "your-client-id") 25CLIENT_SECRET = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET", "your-client-secret") 26ORG_ID = os.getenv("CRIBL_ORGANIZATION_ID", "your-org-id") 27CLOUD_URL = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLOUD_URL", "https://main-your-org.cribl.cloud") 28IP_ALLOWLIST = ["203.0.113.0/24"] 29 30 31def main() -> None: 32 cribl = Cribl( 33 server_url=CLOUD_URL, 34 security=Security(client_id=CLIENT_ID, client_secret=CLIENT_SECRET), 35 ) 36 try: 37 resp = cribl.cloud.api_credentials.create( 38 ORG_ID, 39 name="Auto-Manage-Workspaces", 40 description="Used for automated Workspace management", 41 enabled=True, 42 roles={"organizationRole": "admin"}, 43 ipAllowlist=IP_ALLOWLIST, 44 ) 45 cred = resp.data 46 print(f"Created API Credential name={cred.name!r} clientId={cred.clientId!r}") 47 except AuthenticationError: 48 print("Authentication failed. Check CRIBL_CLIENT_ID and CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET.") 49 except RateLimitError: 50 print("Rate limit reached. Try again in a few seconds.") 51 except APIError as exc: 52 print(f"Request failed: {exc.message}") 53 finally: 54 cribl.close() 55 56 57if __name__ == "__main__": 58 main()

title: Cribl.Cloud billing example · Cribl.Cloud
content:
Guides › Examples › Cribl.Cloud Platform Cribl.Cloud billing example# Cribl.Cloud example_cloud_billing.py
Prints the Organization’s credit balance and lists its credit grants.
To get Client ID and Secret: https://docs.cribl.io/cribl-as-code/sdks-auth/#sdks-auth-cloud
This example is for Cribl.Cloud only. It calls cribl.cloud.billing.* (gateway), not the control-plane /api/v1 APIs.
Prerequisites# pip install cribl-python-sdk CRIBL_CLIENT_ID, CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET CRIBL_ORGANIZATION_ID CRIBL_CLOUD_URL (workspace origin; still required by the client constructor) Environment variables# Variable Default CRIBL_CLIENT_ID your-client-id CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET your-client-secret CRIBL_ORGANIZATION_ID your-org-id CRIBL_CLOUD_URL https://main-your-org.cribl.cloud Code# Python Line numbers Copy code Download .py 17import asyncio 18import os 19 20from cribl_python_sdk import APIError, Cribl, Security 21 22CLIENT_ID = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLIENT_ID", "your-client-id") 23CLIENT_SECRET = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLIENT_SECRET", "your-client-secret") 24ORG_ID = os.getenv("CRIBL_ORGANIZATION_ID", "your-org-id") 25CLOUD_URL = os.getenv("CRIBL_CLOUD_URL", "https://main-your-org.cribl.cloud") 26 27 28async def main() -> None: 29 cribl = Cribl( 30 server_url=CLOUD_URL, 31 security=Security(client_id=CLIENT_ID, client_secret=CLIENT_SECRET), 32 ) 33 try: 34 stats = await cribl.cloud.billing.credits.stats.list_async(ORG_ID) 35 print(f"Credits used: {stats.data.totalCreditsUsed}, remaining: {stats.data.totalCreditsRemaining}") 36 37 grants = await cribl.cloud.billing.credits.grants.list_async(ORG_ID) 38 for grant in grants.data.items: 39 print(f" - {grant.date}: {grant.creditsAcquired} credits ({grant.type})") 40 except APIError as exc: 41 print(f"Request failed: {exc.message}") 42 finally: 43 await cribl.close_async() 44 45 46if __name__ == "__main__": 47 asyncio.run(main())

title: PqType
content:
Persistent queue settings for this Source.
Fields# Field Type Required Description mode Literal["smart", "always"] | None No With Smart mode (deprecated), PQ will write events to the filesystem only when it detects backpressure from the processing engine. Smart mode will have no new development starting July 2026, followed by End of Support and feature removal (auto-migrating to Always On) in January 2027. We recommend using Always On mode instead. With Always On mode, PQ will always write events directly to the queue before forwarding them to the processing engine. maxBufferSizeBytes str | None No The maximum size to hold in memory before writing events to disk. Enter a numeral with units of KB, MB, etc. The minimum value is 64KB and the maximum value is 10MB. maxBufferSize float | None No Maximum number of events to hold in memory before writing the events to disk. Deprecated and only supported in workers < v4.17.0. Use maxBufferSizeBytes instead. commitFrequency float | None No The number of events to send downstream before committing that Stream has read them. Lower values increase cursor-write IOPS and can add disk pressure, including on shared storage. maxFileSize str | None No The maximum size to store in each queue file before closing and optionally compressing. Enter a numeral with units of KB, MB, etc. maxSize str | None No The maximum disk space that the queue can consume (as an average per Worker Process) before queueing stops. Enter a numeral with units of KB, MB, etc. path str | None No The location for the persistent queue files. To this field’s value, the system will append: //inputs/ compress Literal["none", "gzip"] | None No Codec to use to compress the persisted data onBackpressure Literal["block", "drop"] | None No Whether to block or drop events when the queue is exerting backpressure (full capacity or low disk). ‘Block’ is the same behavior as non-PQ blocking. ‘Drop new data’ throws away incoming data, while leaving the contents of the PQ unchanged. pqControls dict[str, Any] | None No Management controls for the persistent queue.
